newsitem.title: USA: One police officer injured as UPS protests heat up.
newsitem.headline: One police officer injured as UPS protests heat up.

text.p: At least one police officer was injured when striking United Parcel Service workers tried to prevent returning trucks from entering a shipping center in the Boston area Tuesday afternoon.

At a second Boston-area facility in Watertown, an orderly protest turned violent as striking Teamsters clashed with police, who were able to maintain a small wedge to allow the returning brown trucks to enter the warehouse.
Watertown police reported no arrests or injuries.

But in nearby Somerville, one police officer was bitten and a worker injured her arm as strikers clashed with some two dozen police trying to make room for seven returning trucks driven by management.
"Scabs," the strikers shouted and several tried to physically block the trucks as they returned.
Somerville police reported a total of eight people were arrested on disorderly conduct charges on Tuesday.
The Teamsters union represents 185,000 workers nationwide who sort, load, pickup and deliver shipments in the well-known UPS brown vans.
The union and UPS remained far apart over workers' demands for better health and pension benefits, higher pay and restrictions on part-time workers and non-union subcontractors.
No new talks had been scheduled.
